title: The Lord Will Happiness Divine
description: The Lord Will Happiness Divine in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 64, “The contrite heart. Isa 47:15”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Lord will happ-i-ness di-vine On con-trite hearts be-stow: Then tell me, gra-cious God, is mine A con-trite heart, or no?

lines: The Lord will happiness divine
On contrite hearts bestow:
Then tell me, gracious God, is mine
A contrite heart, or no?
I hear, but seem to hear in vain,
Insensible as steel;
If ought is felt, 'tis only pain,
To find I cannot feel.
I sometimes think myself inclined
To love thee, if I could;
But often feel another mind,
Averse to all that's good.
My best desires are faint and few,
I fain would strive for more;
But when I cry, "My strength renew,"
Seem weaker than before.
Thy saints are comforted I know,
And love thy house of prayer;
I therefore go where others go,
But find no comfort there.
O make this heart rejoice, or ache;
Decide this doubt for me;
And if it be not broken, break,
And heal it, if it be.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
